56: def _oriented_frame(image: Image.Image) -> tuple[Image.Image, tuple[float, float]]:
57:     """Apply the EXIF orientation to a frame and return it with its DPI axes.
58: 
59:     A camera stores the sensor readout and an orientation tag rather than
60:     rotated pixels, so a portrait photo reaches OCR and layout on its side
61:     unless the tag is honoured. ``exif_transpose`` swaps width and height for
62:     the quarter-turn orientations but leaves ``info["dpi"]`` alone, so the axes
63:     are swapped here whenever it actually rotated the frame.
64:     """
65:     dpi_x, dpi_y = _get_frame_dpi(image)
66:     oriented = ImageOps.exif_transpose(image)
67:     if oriented.size != image.size:
68:         dpi_x, dpi_y = dpi_y, dpi_x
69:     return oriented, (dpi_x, dpi_y)

165: def _rect_to_display_frame(
166:     rect: tuple[float, float, float, float],
167:     rotation: int,
168:     page_size: Size,
169:     origin: tuple[float, float],
170: ) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
171:     """Map a rect from the page's unrotated frame to its rotated display frame.
172: 
173:     PDFium reports page-object and text coordinates in the unrotated PDF user
174:     space, ignoring the page's ``/Rotate`` entry and the position of its visible
175:     box. ``PdfPage.get_size()`` and the rendered page bitmap, on the other hand,
176:     are relative to the visible box (``PdfPage.get_bbox()``) and already in the
177:     rotated display frame. Moving the rect to the box origin and applying the
178:     rotation here puts everything the backend returns into that single frame.
179: 
180:     Args:
181:         rect: ``(x0, y0, x1, y1)`` in the unrotated frame, bottom-left origin.
182:         rotation: page rotation in degrees (``PdfPage.get_rotation()``).
183:         page_size: page size in the display frame (``get_size()``).
184:         origin: lower-left corner of the visible page box in the unrotated
185:             frame (``PdfPage.get_bbox()[:2]``).
186: 
187:     Returns:
188:         ``(x0, y0, x1, y1)`` in the display frame, bottom-left origin.
189:     """
190:     x0, y0, x1, y1 = rect
191:     ox, oy = origin
192:     x0, y0, x1, y1 = x0 - ox, y0 - oy, x1 - ox, y1 - oy
193:     if rotation == 90:
194:         return (y0, page_size.height - x1, y1, page_size.height - x0)
195:     elif rotation == 180:
196:         return (
197:             page_size.width - x1,
198:             page_size.height - y1,
199:             page_size.width - x0,
200:             page_size.height - y0,
201:         )
202:     elif rotation == 270:
203:         return (page_size.width - y1, x0, page_size.width - y0, x1)
204:     return (x0, y0, x1, y1)

12: def rotate_bounding_box(
13:     bbox: BoundingBox, angle: int, im_size: Tuple[int, int]
14: ) -> BoundingRectangle:
15:     # The box is left top width height in TOPLEFT coordinates
16:     # Bounding rectangle start with r_0 at the bottom left whatever the
17:     # coordinate system. Then other corners are found rotating counterclockwise
18:     bbox = bbox.to_top_left_origin(im_size[1])
19:     left, top, width, height = bbox.l, bbox.t, bbox.width, bbox.height
20:     im_w, im_h = im_size
21:     angle = angle % 360
22:     if angle == 0:
23:         return BoundingRectangle.from_bounding_box(bbox)
24:     elif angle == 90:
25:         r_x0 = top + height
26:         r_y0 = im_w - left
27:         r_x1 = r_x0
28:         r_y1 = r_y0 - width
29:         r_x2 = r_x1 - height
30:         r_y2 = r_y1
31:         r_x3 = r_x2
32:         r_y3 = r_y0
33:     elif angle == 180:
34:         r_x0 = im_w - left
35:         r_y0 = im_h - (top + height)
36:         r_x1 = r_x0 - width
37:         r_y1 = r_y0
38:         r_x2 = r_x1
39:         r_y2 = r_y1 + height
40:         r_x3 = r_x0
41:         r_y3 = r_y2
42:     elif angle == 270:
43:         r_x0 = im_h - (top + height)
44:         r_y0 = left
45:         r_x1 = r_x0
46:         r_y1 = r_y0 + width
47:         r_x2 = r_x1 + height
48:         r_y2 = r_y1
49:         r_x3 = r_x2
50:         r_y3 = r_y0
51:     else:
52:         msg = (
53:             f"invalid orientation {angle}, expected values in:"
54:             f" {sorted(CLIPPED_ORIENTATIONS)}"
55:         )
56:         raise ValueError(msg)
57:     rectangle = BoundingRectangle(
58:         r_x0=r_x0,
59:         r_y0=r_y0,
60:         r_x1=r_x1,
61:         r_y1=r_y1,
62:         r_x2=r_x2,
63:         r_y2=r_y2,
64:         r_x3=r_x3,
65:         r_y3=r_y3,
66:         coord_origin=CoordOrigin.TOPLEFT,
67:     )
68:     return rectangle

137:         """Calculate the angle of the rectangle in radians (0-2pi range)."""
138:         p_0 = ((self.r_x0 + self.r_x3) / 2.0, (self.r_y0 + self.r_y3) / 2.0)
139:         p_1 = ((self.r_x1 + self.r_x2) / 2.0, (self.r_y1 + self.r_y2) / 2.0)

149:         else:
150:             angle = math.atan(delta_y / delta_x)
151:         if delta_x < 0:
152:             angle += np.pi
153:         angle = angle % (2 * np.pi)
